page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 24 physical cores yielding 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, backed by 188.0 GB of RAM (3.91 GB per core) and 32 MB of L3 cache. System storage consists of 960 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, while GPU acceleration is not present on this instance type.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core processing capabilities, reflected in top-tier performance for multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Single-core processing and memory bandwidth benchmark results remain within average performance bands. Database execution benchmarks show high throughput, demonstrated by 62.09 million Redis SET operations per second and high scores in PassMark database operations. Small-model LLM text generation speed also falls within top percentiles.

The dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable compute performance without CPU credit constraints or shared-core contention. Although single-threaded speeds are moderate, the combination of 48 dedicated vCPUs, balanced system memory, and local NVMe storage delivers reliable hardware density. This server type is suited for multi-threaded software compilation, database clusters, backend web infrastructure, and CPU-bound machine learning tasks.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated CPU server provisioned with 48 vCPUs from 24 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 188.0 GB of RAM and 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on x86_64 architecture under the QEMU hypervisor, it features 32 MB L3 cache alongside AES, SHA_NI, and AVX instruction sets. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate strong multi-core processing power, achieving top-tier performance in multi-threaded stress-ng, PassMark CPU execution, and software compilation tasks. Database throughput is notable, reaching over 62 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-threaded speed and memory bandwidth fall within average ranges, the dedicated vCPU model and high core count ensure consistent throughput. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, database operations, backend web application clusters, and small-model LLM text generation.
